articles.title: Giannis Leads Heat Past Rockets Amid Bam Injury, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Durant, Top Players
articles.summary: There was good news and there was bad news for the Miami Heat on Monday night.
articles.body:
There was good news and there was bad news for the Miami Heat on Monday night.

The good news was that the team cruised to a 128-110 victory over the Houston Rockets. The bad news was that star center Bam Adebayo didn't play in the second half due to hip tightness.

The hope, obviously, is that the injury is a minor one and his second-half absence was precautionary. In either event, the Heat pulled off the win against a tough Houston team. Here's a look at the game's key performers

Giannis Antetokounmpo helped pick up the slack in the second half after he got off to a slow offensive start in the first two quarters.

It helped that Klay Thompson was on fire from three (5-of-8). And the Heat's backups were superb, outscoring Houston's second unit by a 57-38 margin.

Any team is tough to beat if they hit 18 threes or dish out 29 assists like Miami did on Monday night.

The Heat, if you'll excuse the pun, are red hot at the moment. The win over the Rockets made it five straight victories for Miami (8-6) after a 3-6 start to the season. The Giannis Era may have gotten off to a rocky start, but the Heat appear to have turned a corner, and just in time for Wednesday's matchup against Antetokounmpo's former team, the Milwaukee Bucks.

The Rockets (11-4), meanwhile, have been far better this year than they looked on Monday night. They'll look to rebound on Wednesday against the Indiana Pacers.

articles.title: Bam Adebayo leaves win over Rockets early with hip injury, Heat don't expect long-term issue
articles.summary: Despite losing Bam Adebayo in the second half, the Heat still rolled to a 128-110 win over the Rockets on Monday night.
articles.body:
Bam Adebayo left Monday night's game against the Houston Rockets early with an apparent hip injury.

The Miami Heat star did not take the court to start the second half of their 128-110 victory over the Rockets at the Kaseya Center on Monday, and was instead replaced by Andrew Wiggins to open the third quarter. It didn't appear as if anything happened to Adebayo in the first half, but he was not spotted on the bench as play resumed.

Eventually, the Heat said he was questionable to return with right hip tightness. They then ruled him out for good in the fourth quarter. Further specifics of the injury are not yet known.

Adebayo finished the night with just four points and two assists while shooting 1 of 3 from the field. He entered the night averaging 19.5 points and 8.5 rebounds per contest this season.

Heat coach Erik Spoelstra said after the game that the team was being "proactive" in holding Adebayo out, and that he didn't expect it to be a long-term issue, according to the Miami Herald's Anthony Chiang .

"I saw how he was grinding through it in the second quarter," Spoelstra said, via ESPN . "No matter what he says and no matter what anybody says, let's sit him down and evaluate him tomorrow."

While they don't have specifics yet, losing Adebayo for an extended amount of time would undoubtedly make a major impact on the Heat. Despite losing him, the Heat still managed to roll to a convincing win over the Rockets.

Miami led nearly the entire way on Monday night. The Heat carried a 16-point lead into the locker room at halftime and just cruised the rest of the way to secure the 18-point victory. Giannis Antetokounmpo led the way with 20 points, 16 rebounds and 6 assists. Klay Thompson added 17 points after going 5 of 10 from the 3-point line, and Wiggins had 17 points and five rebounds after stepping in for Adebayo in the second half. The Heat have now won five straight, and sit at 8-6 on the season.

Alperen Sengun led the Rockets with 23 points and seven rebounds. Kevin Durant finished with 22 points, and Jabari Smith Jr. had 12 points and 10 rebounds. The loss dropped them to 11-4 on the year.

articles.title: Bill Fennelly: Iowa State head coach suspended for one game for pushing Sienna Harvey on head
articles.summary: University basketball coach Bill Fennelly is given a one-game suspension for pushing a female player on the head during a timeout.
articles.body:
A university basketball coach in the United States has been given a one-game suspension for pushing a female player on the head during a timeout.

Players were huddled around Iowa State women's coach Bill Fennelly during a fourth-quarter timeout on Sunday when the 69-year-old spoke to guard Sienna Harvey and pushed her on the forehead.

Australian Harvey did not react to the incident, and the Iowa State Cyclones won 69-64 against the University of Illinois-Chicago Flames.

Following the game, Iowa State athletics took disciplinary action against Fennelly, who is now suspended for the Cyclones' next fixture against Northern Iowa on Wednesday.

Fennelly apologised to Harvey, her family and team-mates and said he had allowed his emotions to get the better of him.

"I fully recognise that there are no situations where it is appropriate to make contact with a student-athlete in that way," he said in a statement.

"I accept responsibility and will serve the suspension and I will do better moving forward."

Iowa State athletic director Jared Benko said: "We cannot tolerate inappropriate contact between a coach or staff member and a student-athlete in practice or in competition, whether intentional or not."

Fennelly, who joined Iowa State as women's head coach in 1995, announced in October he plans to retire at the end of the season - his 32nd with the Cyclones.

articles.title: Warriors’ head coach Steve Kerr breaks silence on Stephen Curry’s recovery as the team prepares to navigate his absence
articles.summary: Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors’ star player, recorded an impressive performance in the ongoing season before he sustained a brutal injury and
articles.body: Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors’ star player, recorded an impressive performance in the ongoing season before he sustained a brutal injury and was sidelined. While the Golden State Warriors lost against the New Orleans Pelicans and are gearing up to face the Dallas Mavericks, the team’s head coach Steve Kerr has reflected on Stephen Curry’s situation.Golden State Warriors’ head coach Steve Kerr makes an update about Stephen Curry’s return timeline as he deals with his brutal injuryA few hours ago, the Golden State Warriors’ head coach Steve Kerr spoke to reporters as he said, "I've not talked to him, but I've talked to Rick [Celebrini]. We'll have an update for you on Thanksgiving…Good try, though."This has now sparked widespread concern about Stephen Curry’s health as the reports about his recovery have been pretty conflicting.As per reports, the Golden State Warriors had earlier confirmed that the team would re-evaluate Stephen Curry around the end of November.However, NBA insider Shams Charania has indicated in a recent report that Stephen Curry will most likely stay away from the court for over a month.For the unversed, Stephen Curry suffered the injury during the first quarter of the game against the Houston Rockets on November 11, 2026, after tangling with Alperen Şengün and twisting his trunk.Later, the four time NBA champion underwent an MRI which confirmed a right oblique abdominal tear. Since then, Stephen Curry left the team's road trip to return to San Francisco to work directly with the team’s director of sports medicine and performance Rick Celebrini.Golden State Warriors’ locker room remains tensed about Stephen Curry’s situation as they gear up to adjust to his absenceA few days ago, The Athletic’s Nick Friedell reflected on how the Golden State Warriors’ locker room reacted as the team awaited MRI results.In an appearance on the Warriors Plus Minus podcast, The Athletic’s Nick Friedell said, "Jim, the vibe is that it sounded as if his teammates were hoping for the best, and Kerr, as he said, he's hoping for the best, but nobody knows…”The Athletic’s Nick Friedell added, “The feel, though, was these guys were kind of like, 'All right, we've been through this.' They didn't certainly think it would be too dramatic, but nobody's gonna know until we hear the MRI results, but the takeaway was they're expecting to be without him at least for a short period amount of time, and hopefully that's it."The Athletic’s Nick Friedell continued, "Draymond and Podz, I had the same message, which is, hey, we've been through this. We're better equipped to handle the Steph absence. This year, with Yaxel, with the pieces in place now, than they were a year ago, or h*ll, 6 months ago…”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Bam Adebayo injury update: Latest on Miami Heat star’s health after Rockets win
articles.summary: Bam Adebayo sat out the second half of Miami’s 128-110 win over the Houston Rockets on Monday night because of right hip tightness.
articles.body: Bam Adebayo sat out the second half of Miami’s 128-110 win over the Houston Rockets on Monday night because of right hip tightness. The Heat first listed him as questionable before ruling the 29-year-old center out for the night. Adebayo played about 16 minutes at Kaseya Center and scored four points with two steals. The win was Miami’s fifth in a row, but the early exit took some shine off it. Coach Erik Spoelstra has since given his read on how serious the problem is, and the Heat host Milwaukee on Wednesday.How serious is Bam Adebayo’s hip injury?Spoelstra does not expect a long absence. The coach called the move proactive and said he watched Adebayo push through the second quarter, then decided the night was over no matter what anyone said. “I don’t think it’s long term,” Spoelstra said.Miami has not named a diagnosis beyond right hip tightness or given a return date. The plan was to see how Adebayo felt the next day. Adebayo’s availability for Wednesday’s home game against Milwaukee is unclear.Adebayo came into Monday averaging 19.5 points, 8.5 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 2.1 steals. A slow offensive start to the season had given way to better chemistry next to Giannis Antetokounmpo, including 37 points and 14 rebounds against Cleveland on Friday. Against Houston, Adebayo took only three shots in the first half but finished plus-9 as Miami built a 62-46 lead by the break.Antetokounmpo and Wiggins cover for AdebayoSpoelstra shifted Antetokounmpo to center and gave Andrew Wiggins the open starting spot to begin the second half. Wiggins finished with 17 points on 6-of-9 shooting, five rebounds and three blocks, and Miami was plus-15 with him on the floor. Antetokounmpo had 20 points, 13 rebounds, six assists and three blocks in roughly 29 minutes, including 14 points in the third quarter, before sitting out the fourth of the blowout.Spoelstra said Antetokounmpo set the tone on offense, finding teammates like Magic Johnson through the opening 14 minutes. The loss goes beyond points, since Adebayo anchors the defense with rim protection, rebounding and the range to guard several positions.The Heat were also without Pelle Larsson, who missed a third straight game with an illness and is expected to be back Wednesday. Across the five-game run, Miami has posted a 126.2 offensive rating, second in the league, and a net rating of 12.5, fourth best. The defense ranks 10th at 113.7, and Spoelstra liked what he saw after holding Houston to 110.Miami is 8-6 after five straight wins and hosts the 1-13 Bucks on Wednesday in Antetokounmpo’s first game against his former franchise.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “I saw a different side of him”: Dwight Howard reflects on what Kobe Bryant loved doing years after his tragic death
articles.summary: It has been close to seven years since the NBA icon Kobe Bryant left the world mourning for him and his young daughter as the two passed away in a tragic
articles.body: It has been close to seven years since the NBA icon Kobe Bryant left the world mourning for him and his young daughter as the two passed away in a tragic helicopter crash in 2020. While his wife, Vanessa Bryant, has kept working on what he has left behind, his former teammate, Dwight Howard, has shared an emotional memory related to him.Dwight Howard reflects on an emotional memory he shared with Kobe Bryant years before his tragic deathA few hours ago, NBA legend Dwight Howard made an appearance on the Men's Health Strong Talk, where he reflected on his memories with Kobe Bryant and said, "I got to see a different side of him. I didn't know he liked the movie – I always say this – Pitch Perfect. "I always remember that. He loved Pitch Perfect. I was shocked. He was like, 'You know, I love Pitch Perfect.' I was like, 'What?'"The former Los Angeles Lakers’ icon Dwight Howard reflected on the time when Kobe Bryant suffered an injury as he said, "When he tore his Achilles, we drove out to his house, which was so far. I was like, 'Oh my God, like he lived next to heaven or something. Why does it take so long for us to get to his house?' "We get to his house, and we're just like: 'Hey man, we wanted to come and check on you, make sure you're okay or whatever.' "I know how it feels having a surgery and having to be out when you want to stay and play and stuff like that. So I just wanted to come check on him.”Dwight Howard added, "And that's when I found out he likes Pitch Perfect. He was talking about it, he was just watching the movie. Every time I think about Kobe, I think about Pitch Perfect, so it's crazy."While Kobe Bryant’s wife Vanessa Bryant has not reacted to Dwight Howard’s words yet, his confession has made many fans emotional.Interestingly, this was not the first time that Dwight Howard has spoken about his fond memories with Kobe Bryant.Kobe Bryant’s wife Vanessa Bryant continues her philanthropic activitiesThe Los Angeles Lakers’ icon has often spoken about the conversations they have had and how their bond remained strong for years.It has been over six years since Kobe Bryant tragically passed away in January 2020. His family and especially his wife, Natalia Bryant has remained pretty strong and has stepped up to be there for their children as they dealt with the loss of a parent and a sibling at a young age.Today, Kobe Bryant’s wife Vanessa Bryant has become a popular philanthropist and continues to work towards disadvantaged communities across the nation while their oldest daughter have turned into a popular model.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Is Luka Doncic already matching prime LeBron James? Former Cavaliers teammate offers his definitive take
articles.summary: Luka Doncic is averaging 39.0 points per game, and DeMarcus Cousins believes the Los Angeles Lakers superstar has not hit his ceiling.
articles.body: Luka Doncic is averaging 39.0 points per game, and DeMarcus Cousins believes the Los Angeles Lakers superstar has not hit his ceiling. The former All-Star made the case on Gil’s Arena, where he argued with Gilbert Arenas over a hypothetical: Doncic’s Lakers against LeBron James and the 2007 Cleveland Cavaliers. Arenas took James, whom he faced in the playoffs. Cousins took Doncic, and he expects bigger scoring nights once the Lakers star reaches midseason form. The Lakers are 12-2 after eight straight wins, with Doncic putting up 43 against the Phoenix Suns last Sunday.Is Luka Doncic already on prime LeBron James’ level?Nobody in the debate claimed Luka Doncic has passed LeBron James. DeMarcus Cousins and Arenas were arguing over how a team built around each star would fare. James carried a thin Cleveland roster to the 2007 NBA Finals in his fourth season, and Arenas wanted that version respected.His point was simple. Most people picture a 30-year-old or 40-year-old James, not the 21- or 22-year-old he played against. “Who the f*** is stopping LeBron James?” Arenas asked.Cousins first asked whether the point was stopping James or containing him. He agreed James is incredible. Still, Cousins sees “nothing that can stop Luka” out there.Both teams leaned hard on one star, so the matchup is tough to settle on paper. Cleveland does not reach the Finals without James.The gap between the two cases is clear. James has a Finals trip from 2007. Doncic has a 12-2 start and the best 12-game scoring total in 50 years, but the season is only 14 games old.Doncic’s numbers back up Cousins’ 100-point talkCousins also believes Doncic is only warming up. He would not be shocked by a 100-point game from Doncic soon, and he named Wilt Chamberlain’s record as the mark in play.The numbers make the talk reasonable. Doncic has 468 points through 12 games, the most for any player over that span in 50 years. Seven of those games went for 40 or more, which is 25 percent of all 40-point games league-wide this season. He has two 50-point nights, and his lowest total is 23.Doncic averaged 36.2 points in October and has pushed that to 41.0 in November, shooting 49.4 percent from the field, 41.8 percent from three and 85.9 percent at the line. If the 39.0 average holds, he joins Michael Jordan, Kobe Bryant and James Harden as the only players to average 35 or more in a season since 1980.Tim Hardaway sees it the same way, with a condition. He said if anyone can get there, it is Doncic, but health decides it. Doncic played only 50 and 64 games in the last two seasons.Doncic was not sold when Cousins asked him about 100 at the 2026 All-Star weekend. “I scored 73, and it was a lot,” he said. Nine months on, he is hotter, and the Lakers roster around him fits his scoring better.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
